subject: Capacity commitments & cost targets for Q3 pipeline
messages:
From: Andrew King <andrew.king@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@cloudscale.io
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — Q3 capacity ask

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we have a rough internal plan for a paid pilot that would start late July. Finance asked me to get a committed capacity proposal so they can map ARR. The ask: 4k concurrent tokens/day (production, low-latency), spike allowance 2x for launch week, and sandbox embeddings for 2 engineers.

We'd like a 6-month reserved capacity quote with clear burst behavior and an estimate of unit cost after batching and prefix caching. Can your team confirm whether the dedicated offering can guarantee these latency SLOs for their initial load?

Happy to join a short call this week.

—Andrew
Head of Data Products, Nimbus Analytics

Attachments: NIM-q3-intake.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Andrew King <andrew.king@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — Q3 capacity ask

Andrew — thanks for the clarity. Looping in Ben (fleet planning) and Laura (finance) to align on commitment sizing and pricing. High level:

- We can support a reserved pool sized for 4k concurrent tokens/day for production (target p95 latency < 180ms with our optimized runtime) assuming model selection M-7b-quant and standard prefix caching.
- Burst allowance: we support 2x burst via burst credits on Dedicated; need to confirm burst slot counts for your initial week.
- Sandbox/embedding: we can host dev embeddings on isolated lower-tier nodes.

Action items:
1) Ben — can you confirm GPU count and expected throughput for this profile and whether current commitments allow the 2x burst?
2) Laura — draft a 6-month reserved quote with one-time onboarding + estimated per-token cost after planned batching.
3) Andrew — share expected peak concurrent requests/day in tokens and any model preference.

I'll schedule a 30-min alignment standup tomorrow 10:30 AM PT.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | m: 415-555-0123

Attachments: NIM-q3-forecast-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Andrew King <andrew.king@nimbus-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — Q3 capacity ask

On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 11:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Andrew — thanks for the clarity. Looping in Ben (fleet planning) and Laura (finance) to align on commitment sizing and pricing.

Thanks — read through the intake quickly. Short answers:
- For an M-7b-quant baseline to hit p95 < 180ms we expect ~8 A100-equivalent slots for steady-state serving at the 4k concurrent tokens/day target (assuming continuous arrival & our batching profile).
- To support 2x burst for launch week we need to reserve 4 additional burst-capable slots (burst credits can be consumed from a shared pool but for guaranteed performance we recommend reserving explicit burst-capacity).
- If they want better latency headroom (p95 < 140ms), bump to 12 slots or switch to a smaller sequence length model with lower kernel cost.

Constraints: we currently have a couple of reserved commitments that overlap that reduce our unallocated pool for July by ~25%. Karthik — can you surface any near-term expirations or reassignable pools?

Proposed next steps:
- Mine the forecast spreadsheet Andrew attached to produce a heatmap of token arrival by week.
- Produce two commitment scenarios: conservative (reserve minimal + burst credits) and aggressive (reserve burst slots upfront).

I'll put a short runbook together and attach the fleet run-rate file.

—Ben
Fleet Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: fleet-cost-model-2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Andrew King <andrew.king@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — Q3 capacity ask

Hi all — quick finance framing before the call:

Summary (6-month commitment):
- Base reserved fee (incl. onboarding): $58,000/month
- Estimated variable token cost after batching & caching: $0.00035/token (production), $0.00012/token (sandbox embeddings) — this assumes the conservative batch profile Ben referenced.
- One-time onboarding and SOC2 evidence collection: $12,500

Simple cost scenarios based on expected token run-rates Andrew provided in the sheet: 
- Low: 3.2M tokens/day => ~$80k/month incl. reserved fee
- Mid: 4.0M tokens/day => ~$98k/month
- High: 6.5M tokens/day (post-launch spike sustained) => ~$145k/month

Finance asks:
1) Confirm whether burst slots will incur additional monthly charge or be paid from a prepaid burst-credit bucket. (Ben)
2) Confirm whether we can cap effective spend per day via autoscale/fallback policies so Nimbus has a hard spend limit during launch. (Karthik)

I'll have a draft term sheet for the 6-month commitment ready after we pick conservative vs aggressive.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

On attachments: I referenced the forecast and fleet model in my calculations. I also added a one-page term summary to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bForecast

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Andrew King <andrew.king@nimbus-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — Q3 capacity ask

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Recap + action items (short):

Recap:
- Fleet baseline: 8 A100-equiv slots for steady state at M-7b-quant; +4 burst slots recommended for guaranteed launch-week headroom.
- Finance: monthly committed fee + variable tokens as Laura outlined; two scenario quotes (conservative/aggressive).
- Ops: autoscale + fallback policy can enforce a hard daily spend cap; will document trade-offs.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: attach the runbook & two scenario slot allocations in Drive (by Tue EOD). (Attachment: fleet-runbook-v1.md)
- Laura: publish draft term sheet + price sheet for conservative/aggressive (by Tue noon).
- Karthik: confirm reassignable pool & any expirations that free capacity in July (by Tue 11 AM).
- Mina/Andrew: 30-min standup tomorrow 10:30 AM PT to agree on scenario and sign-off path.

Andrew — please confirm the final preferred model and whether Nimbus wants the burst slots reserved as part of the commitment or via a prepaid credit. If you prefer a single doc, we'll drop the 6-month PS and the term sheet into the Drive link above for review.

Cheers,
Mina
